title: Co-marketing playbook: finding partners and planning joint campaigns
summary: Corey Haines' open-source co-marketing skill lays out how to pick partners who share your audience but not your budget, score them, choose among five partnership types, and structure and measure joint campaigns. It is an AI agent playbook, so it reads as a checklist-style framework rather than narrative advice.

principles.text: Best partners share your audience but don't compete for the same budget.
principles.quote: The best partners share your audience but don't compete for the same budget.

principles.text: Pick partners adjacent in the workflow: same buyer, different problem, complementary not competitive.
principles.quote: Same buyer persona, different problem solved

principles.text: Score candidate partners 1-5 on audience fit, size, brand alignment, engagement, reciprocity and ease of execution.
Co-marketing is one of five partnership types; route to the right play instead of defaulting to joint content.
principles.quote: Co-marketing is one of **five partnership types**. Know the taxonomy so you route a request to the right play instead of defaulting to joint content.

principles.text: Partner programs can drive a large share of revenue; mature programs average about 28% of revenue and 2x growth.
principles.quote: Mature programs average **~28% of revenue and 2× growth**.

principles.text: Go into partner calls with 2-3 specific campaign ideas and a clear ask, not "let's do something."
principles.quote: **2-3 specific campaign ideas** (not just "let's do something")
